key_insight: CSM replaces a single constitutive law with an admissible set and uses the structure’s own strain history to bound and select the robust response.
engineering_relevance: This lets engineers quantify worst-case structural behavior when experiments cannot uniquely identify the material law, improving uncertainty-aware design and certification.
method: Formulate mechanics variationally over a set of admissible constitutive laws instead of one law.
Use the occupation measure of reached strains to turn the set response into a support-function energy.
Solve equilibrium to obtain rigorous upper bounds, with two-sided certificates under global minimization.
evidence_signal: The paper demonstrates CSM on linear elasticity, fracture, a finite-strain composite shell, and a membrane; in one shell case the structure interrogates only 4 of 226 constitutive directions, and the membrane’s certified worst-case energy exceeds the reference by more than 4×.
watch_item: The approach depends on reliable admissible-set specification and can be computationally sensitive when the constitutive space is large or poorly constrained.
paper_title: Constitutive-Set Mechanics: variational mechanics on an admissible set of constitutive laws
